paragraphs.text: Some locations in this account are approximate.
On 17 July 1791, the Champ de Mars Massacre struck a crowd of republican protesters in Paris.
On 10 August 1792, armed revolutionaries stormed the Tuileries Palace, leading France to abolish the monarchy and establish a republic.
The Louvre Museum is dated here to 1793.
The Revolt of 1 Prairial Year III, on 20 May 1795, was the final major popular uprising of the French Revolution.
In 1795, 13 Vendémiaire, a battle in the streets of Paris, advanced the career of Napoleon Bonaparte.
In 1797, the Coup of 18 Fructidor ousted the monarchists from the legislature.
Eugène Delacroix was born here in 1798.
On 9 November 1799, the bloodless Coup of 18 Brumaire overthrew the Directory and brought Napoleon Bonaparte to power as First Consul.
Napoleon Bonaparte and Pope Pius VII signed the Concordat of 1801 in Paris on 15 July 1801.
Napoleon was crowned Emperor of the French on December 2, 1804, at Notre-Dame de Paris.
George Sand was born here in 1804, Alexis de Tocqueville in 1805, and Napoleon III in 1808.
In 1814, Allied forces drove back the defenders of Paris, and the French evacuated it on 31 March.
The Treaty of Paris was signed on 30 May 1814 and the Second Treaty of Paris on 20 November 1815.
